The rider does not press a deviation the trace cannot carry, no exculpatory clause needs to be reached because there is no excess to excuse, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation is not triggered on this record.

claims.text: The governing measurement for the threshold test is the trace polyline: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 22.26 km, and the platform's own derived deviation block records an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.72% of the 22.1 km optimal route, with the status field reading 'no deviation'. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass — an excess greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal. An excess of 0.16 km fails the absolute test five-fold and 0.72% fails the proportional test by a wide margin. No route deviation is established on this trip.

POL-RD-01 forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, but the driver's position does not depend on that rule: even on the rounded field the rider's side would prefer (22.3 km, deviation_pct 0.9 as recorded on the trip record), the excess over the 22.1 km optimal is 0.2 km — a quarter of the 0.8 km absolute threshold — and under 1% against a 20% proportional threshold. On either figure the establishment test fails on both limbs, and POL-RD-01 provides that where either test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The trace is unimpaired both at the schema level (EV-GPS-00528 is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes) and for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage_pct 100, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of limbs (a) to (c) — a gap over 90 seconds, a jump over 500 m, a sustained interval over 30 seconds — is met. The excess is therefore measured from a full-strength trace, no independent corroboration is needed, and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not open.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and must show both that the artifacts describe the same trip and that an excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The second limb fails on every artifact in the bundle — the excess is 0.16 km on the trace and 0.2 km even on the rounded trip-record figure — so the burden never shifts to the driver: he is not required to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12, and an assertion of overcharging that no artifact supports carries no weight.

There is no traffic advisory on file at all: EV-ADVIS-00528-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, has weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING) — that impairment is disclosed, and the artifact can carry no fact; its absence is all that is citable. The driver asserts no queue, closure or incident — his statement on the record is 'Normal trip, normal route. I don't set fares.' — so POL-RD-03 is never invoked and there is no external-cause assertion to test against an advisory. Under POL-RD-13 an advisory that no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not the contradiction with a cited artifact that POL-RD-10(5) escalates on; the missing advisory therefore changes nothing and triggers no escalation.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity line for POL-RD-09(4) to act on: the fare ledger carries erp_gantries [] with tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, and the derived erp_lines block totals 0.00 on-route and 0.00 off-route. Nothing in the fare is a phantom gantry or a wrongly applied surcharge, so there is no standalone correction to make with or without a deviation.

With no deviation established, POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION, and POL-GEN-03 fixes what that means on this record: the present state stands. The ledger records payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and charged_total SGD 44.44. This dispute was filed by the rider, so leaving the present state in place leaves the fare charged and unrefunded — which is the driver's case, not the rider's.

The rider's account of the money matches no artifact: he pleads a SGD 60 estimate and a SGD 91.60 charge, and says a manager refunded the difference plus a voucher, but the fare breakdown shows charged_total SGD 44.44, refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED, and the chat export for this trip contains zero messages. The fare that does exist is internally consistent — base fare 3.80 plus distance 16.73 plus time 10.64 plus the 0.80 platform fee plus surge 12.47 equals 44.44 exactly. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no supporting artifact carries no weight.

The rider's 'no surge' complaint is a complaint about the fare model, not about the route. The surge_multiplier of 1.4 is recorded on EV-FARE-00528 — the only artifact from which the policy permits that figure to be read — and it is applied to base fare, distance charge and time charge, producing the SGD 12.47 surge line. No clause of the route-deviation policy refunds a correctly applied surge where no deviation is established, and POL-RD-02's recomputation does not run at all without one.

Nothing in the driver's record assists the rider. POL-RD-06 is not engaged, because it is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation or the evidence is otherwise finely balanced, and neither condition holds here; and its own counters are silent in any event — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, far below both the '3 or more' limb and the 5% limb. No profile field other than those POL-RD-06 names may be used against him (POL-GEN-01).

ruling.explanation: This decision is addressed to both the rider and the driver. The dispute is a route-deviation claim, so the first question is whether the trip actually deviated from the platform's optimal route. On the governing measurement it did not. POL-RD-01 requires the actual distance to exceed the optimal distance by more than 0.8 km AND by more than 20%; both tests must pass, and if either fails there is no deviation and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00528) is complete and unimpaired — 229 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) do not fire and no independent corroboration is needed. Its trace_distance_km is 22.26 km, and the platform's derived deviation block records an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.72%, against the optimal route of 22.1 km (EV-TRIP-00528). That fails the 0.8 km absolute test by a wide margin and the 20% relative test by a wider one. Even on the rounded trip-record figure the rider's side might prefer (22.3 km), the excess is 0.2 km — still far below both thresholds. On both the driver's and the rider's own submissions the establishment test fails on both limbs, so no deviation is established. I have considered the rider's account that the fare was estimated at about SGD 60 and charged at SGD 91.60 and that a manager refunded the difference plus a voucher. Those figures match no artifact in the bundle. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00528) shows charged_total SGD 44.44, composed of base fare 3.80 + distance 16.73 + time 10.64 + platform fee 0.80 + surge 12.47, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the in-app chat export (EV-CHAT-00528) contains zero messages. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no supporting artifact carries no weight, so these statements cannot move the outcome. The rider's 'no surge' point also fails: the surge_multiplier of 1.4 is recorded on EV-FARE-00528 — the only artifact from which the policy permits that figure to be read — and no clause of the route-deviation policy refunds a correctly applied surge where no deviation is established. I have checked the pass-through lines under POL-RD-09. There are no ERP gantries and no tolls (both totals 0.00) and no airport surcharge (0.0) on a trip that neither starts nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom or double-counted line and no standalone billing-integrity correction to make. The bundle holds no traffic advisory — EV-ADVIS-00528-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0 — but the driver asserts no queue, closure or incident, so POL-RD-03 is never invoked; under POL-RD-13 an advisory that no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not the contradiction with a cited artifact that POL-RD-10(5) escalates on, and it triggers no escalation. No other POL-RD-10 trigger applies: the trip identifiers all match (TRP-00528), the timestamps are consistent, the trace is unimpaired, there is no competing admissible evidence of comparable strength, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. POL-RD-06 is not engaged, as there is no material deviation and the evidence is not finely balanced; its own counters are silent in any event (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250). POL-RD-04 driver compensation does not arise because the billed distance (22.3 km) is not less than the trace distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall. The outcome is accordingly NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands, meaning the fare of SGD 44.44 remains charged and unrefunded. No referral is issued, because no clause produces one. The confidence of 0.9 rests on the trace and trip record, both at full weight 1.0.

Other routes. POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity has nothing to act on — no gantry, toll or surcharge line appears at all — so there is no standalone correction whether or not a deviation exists. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00528-01, is MISSING with weight multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; that impairment is disclosed, no party invoked POL-RD-03 or cited this identifier, and under POL-RD-13(1) an advisory no one has cited is a gap in the bundle, not the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction that escalates.

Driver. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: no MATERIAL deviation was recorded and the evidence is not finely balanced. The fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantry crossings and no tolls (both totals are 0.00) and an airport_surcharge of 0.0 on a trip that neither originates at nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom or double-counted pass-through line, and no gantry line to match against the trace under POL-RD-09 limb (4). The governing measurement for the threshold test is the trace polyline: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 22.26 km, and the platform's own derived deviation block records an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.72% of the 22.1 km optimal route, with the status field reading 'no deviation'. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass — an excess greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal.
